question: Can large-batch off-policy reinforcement learning on synthetic, corpus-grounded search tasks produce an efficient enterprise knowledge agent that generalizes across different retrieval and reasoning regimes and benefits predictably from test-time search?

key_findings.claim: KARL combines a six-regime benchmark, agentic synthetic-data generation, iterative off-policy RL, learned context compression, and test-time search in one enterprise-search system.
key_findings.evidence: KARLBench includes BrowseComp-Plus, TREC-Biogen, FinanceBench, QAMPARI, FreshStack, and the private PMBench; training uses synthetic questions and trajectories from BrowseComp-Plus and TREC-Biogen, with OAPL updates and optional parallel or value-guided inference.

key_findings.claim: Multi-task RL materially improves the base model and parallel inference reaches the best proprietary-model aggregate score.
key_findings.evidence: Table 4 reports GLM-4.5-Air at 52.6 total, single-call KARL at 58.9, parallel N=3 at 64.1, N=10 at 67.5, and N=20 at 68.1; Claude 4.6 Opus scores 67.5 under the paper's best-configuration protocol.

key_findings.claim: Single-task experts do not transfer between the two training task families, while multi-task RL yields a smaller gain on held-out regimes than on the training regimes.
key_findings.evidence: KARL-TREC reaches 85.0 on TREC-Biogen but 42.2 on BrowseComp-Plus; KARL-BCP reaches 59.6 on BrowseComp-Plus but 68.0 on TREC. Multi-task KARL moves the in-distribution aggregate from 55.4 to 69.4 and the OOD aggregate from 51.2 to 53.7 without parallel sampling.

key_findings.claim: The headline OOD generalization remains within the same tool, retrieval, corpus-grounding, and answer-evaluation interface rather than demonstrating arbitrary agent-task transfer.
key_findings.evidence: All six regimes expose vector search and corpus-grounded response generation, while only BrowseComp-Plus and TREC-Biogen provide RL data. The held-out tasks vary query form and corpus, but not the core search-action interface.

key_findings.claim: Evaluation examples and benchmark structure influence synthetic training generation, creating a documented contamination path even with deduplication.
key_findings.evidence: The synthesis pipeline seeds generation with held-out benchmark examples, including four TREC examples, then has agents explore the same corpora and uses GPT-4o-mini or GPT-5-mini for deduplication or quality filtering. BrowseComp calibration and remaining subsets also participate in development decisions.

key_findings.claim: Some benchmark corpora and gold signals make the tasks easier or less independently reproducible than natural enterprise search.
key_findings.evidence: QAMPARI indexes only documents containing at least one gold answer, BrowseComp-Plus's first-512-character corpus setting covers only 86.5% of gold evidence, several nugget sets are LLM-generated, and PMBench contains 57 internal private tasks.

key_findings.claim: The appendix contradicts the main text about whether TREC synthetic data receives a quality filter.
key_findings.evidence: The main setup says GPT-5-mini performs the TREC quality filter and Appendix examples show such a filter, while the data-generation detail on page 53 states that no quality filter is applied for TREC-Biogen.

key_findings.claim: Evaluator independence is incomplete because nuggets, synthetic questions, data filters, and answer scoring are substantially model-generated, and answer scoring does not require citation entailment.
key_findings.evidence: The nugget judge checks the answer against a supplied nugget list but does not verify cited evidence or penalize every unsupported extra statement. Aside from manual verification of private PMBench items, the paper does not report a broad blinded human agreement study for final benchmark scores.

key_findings.claim: Outcome reward is assigned coarsely to every search and compression segment, so successful trajectories do not identify which intermediate actions caused success.
key_findings.evidence: OAPL filters all-correct and all-wrong examples and applies the trajectory outcome to segmented search and compression samples. Compression is included in the policy but its summary may preserve or discard different evidence without direct step-level reward.

key_findings.claim: The cost and latency Pareto comparison is operationally useful but not hardware- or compute-matched.
key_findings.evidence: Hosted systems use provider prices and selected reasoning efforts, KARL uses open-model pricing assumptions and up to 20 parallel trajectories, and latency is measured with KARL on eight H200 GPUs against external APIs. Table 4 reports the best baseline value with or without compression.

key_findings.claim: Max-at-k improvement does not prove that RL creates solutions outside the base model's support.
key_findings.evidence: The paper interprets improved max@k and more successful diverse traces as new capabilities; at finite k, the same observation is also consistent with redistributing probability toward rare solutions already possible under the base model.

key_findings.claim: Human input is not part of the core learning or evaluation loop, and the optional preference interface is not evaluated.
key_findings.evidence: Training uses synthetic prompts, model rollouts, model filters, and outcome rewards; an optional human-preference application appears only at the end of the appendix without user-study results or a reported influence on KARLBench outcomes.

method.core_idea: Train a compact enterprise-search agent from synthetic, long-horizon corpus interactions using iterative large-batch off-policy RL, then scale quality at inference with parallel thinking or value-guided selection.
method.mechanism: A generator explores indexed corpora to construct questions, candidates are deduplicated and quality-filtered, solver models produce multi-step search and compression trajectories, and outcome-based nugget rewards label segments. OAPL performs least-squares off-policy policy updates over large batches across several iterations. Multi-task batches balance token volume between BrowseComp-Plus and TREC-Biogen. At test time the same policy can sample parallel traces and aggregate them, or a Qwen3-4B value model can guide search over candidates.
assumptions: Synthetic questions generated from evaluation-like examples and the same corpora remain sufficiently distinct from test questions.
Nugget recall and correctness faithfully represent grounded enterprise-search usefulness.
Copying outcome reward to search and compression segments supplies adequate credit for long-horizon behavior.
Held-out benchmark regimes sharing one retrieval interface are a meaningful test of general search transfer.
Provider-price and latency measurements are comparable enough to establish Pareto efficiency.
Best-of-configuration baselines and single reported aggregate scores are stable without extensive seed confidence intervals.

techniques.role: Generates grounded training questions by exploring indexed corpora rather than relying only on authored labels.
Reuses large rollout batches through OAPL and refreshes data with progressively trained policies.
Balances training contribution by total tokens across heterogeneous search regimes.
Summarizes retrieved evidence within the policy and receives outcome-derived training signal.
Samples multiple independent research trajectories and aggregates them at test time.
Uses a learned value model to select or expand promising candidate reasoning trajectories.
Scores generated answers against atomic expected facts across heterogeneous question types.

evaluations.setting: KARLBench's six search regimes with unified vector retrieval, comparing open and proprietary models under each model's recommended settings.
evaluations.metric: Unweighted aggregate of regime-specific nugget or task scores.
evaluations.result: GLM-4.5-Air scores 52.6, KARL 58.9, KARL parallel N=10 scores 67.5, and N=20 scores 68.1; Claude 4.6 Opus scores 67.5.
evaluations.baseline: GLM-4.5-Air base model plus Qwen, MiniMax, GPT, and Claude variants.

evaluations.setting: Single-task versus multi-task RL on BrowseComp-Plus and TREC-Biogen with four held-out benchmark regimes.
evaluations.metric: In-distribution, out-of-distribution, and total aggregate score.
evaluations.result: Single-task specialists peak on their own task but fail to cross-transfer; single-call multi-task KARL improves in-distribution from 55.4 to 69.4 and OOD from 51.2 to 53.7.
evaluations.baseline: The GLM-4.5-Air base model and each single-task RL specialist.

evaluations.metric: KARLBench total and OOD aggregate versus test-time trajectory budget.
evaluations.result: Total rises from 58.9 to 64.1, 67.5, and 68.1; OOD rises from 53.7 to 59.6, 62.7, and 63.0.
evaluations.baseline: Single-call KARL and proprietary models at their selected reasoning settings.

evaluations.setting: Multi-expert supervised distillation versus multi-task RL with and without parallel inference.
evaluations.metric: In-distribution and OOD aggregate scaling with additional samples.
evaluations.result: Distillation's OOD score changes only 59.4 to 59.6 under added test-time compute, while KARL's OOD score improves with parallel sampling.
evaluations.baseline: Label-free SFT on rollouts from the two single-task experts.

evaluations.setting: Compression and retrieval-budget ablations plus BrowseComp-Plus value-guided search.
evaluations.metric: Task score as compression, retrieved-result count, and value-guided candidate count change.
evaluations.result: Removing learned compression drops one reported score from 0.570 to 0.389; flooding context with 40 results degrades performance; VGS raises KARL-BCP from 59.6 to 70.4 at N=17.
evaluations.baseline: KARL with learned compression, default retrieval depth, or no value-guided test-time search.

evaluations.setting: Cost-quality and latency-quality comparison across hosted APIs and self-hosted KARL configurations.
evaluations.metric: Estimated dollars per query and wall-clock latency at matched aggregate quality.
evaluations.result: The paper reports single-call KARL below $0.10, N=10 quality matching Claude 4.6 Opus at about 33% lower cost and 47% lower latency.
evaluations.baseline: Published API prices, selected provider reasoning efforts, and latency measurements for proprietary baselines.

limitations: Author-stated: the agent exposes only a single vector-search tool and future work should broaden action spaces and improve context management.
Reviewer inference: all OOD tasks retain the same corpus-search and response interface, so transfer beyond knowledge retrieval is untested.
Reviewer inference: evaluation examples seed synthetic generation and LLM deduplication is fallible, leaving residual benchmark contamination.
Reviewer inference: QAMPARI's oracle-filtered corpus and generated nugget sets do not fully represent open-world recall and ground-truth uncertainty.
Reviewer inference: PMBench is private, preventing independent reproduction of one sixth of the benchmark aggregate.
Reviewer inference: nugget-based scoring does not require evidence citation or consistently penalize unsupported additions, weakening grounded-answer validity.
Reviewer inference: quality tables do not report sufficient random-seed confidence intervals, and baseline reasoning, compression, hardware, and test-time compute are not factorially matched.
Reviewer inference: cost estimates compare hosted prices with self-hosting assumptions and parallel hardware, so the Pareto frontier is deployment-specific.
Reviewer inference: outcome reward copied to every trajectory segment supplies weak causal credit and can reinforce incidental search or lossy compression behavior.
Reviewer inference: no evaluated human-in-the-loop condition establishes whether human curation, correction, or preferences improve safety and factual grounding.
failure_modes: Synthetic questions can paraphrase or preserve evaluation structure despite LLM deduplication.
An agent can retrieve the right evidence but receive a low score because compression anchors on an outdated snippet and discards a later correction.
A fluent answer can satisfy nuggets while adding unsupported details or failing a hidden constraint.
An oracle-filtered retrieval corpus can make exhaustive-answer performance look better than real corpus discovery.
A single-task RL expert can over-specialize and fail even on the other nominally in-distribution task.
Test-time max@k gains can be misinterpreted as newly created support rather than increased probability of rare existing solutions.
Best-of-many parallel trajectories can improve quality while concealing high total inference compute and tail latency.
A value model trained on outcome-correlated traces can select benchmark shortcuts rather than genuinely grounded reasoning.
Numerical synthesis can fail even when relevant evidence is retrieved, and binary final-answer scoring may miss reasoning-constraint violations.
reusable_insights: Evaluate synthetic-data RL on benchmark formats, corpora, tools, and model families held out jointly, not one axis at a time.
Separate retrieval recall, evidence entailment, compression fidelity, reasoning validity, and final-answer correctness in the reward.
Use independent human-authored hidden questions and blinded judge audits to detect synthesis-to-evaluation circularity.
Report single-sample quality, quality-versus-total-compute curves, and ranking stability across inference budgets rather than only a Pareto envelope.
Treat max@k improvement as probability-mass evidence unless new support is established with stronger counterfactual tests.
Add segment-level counterfactual rewards or ablations so successful outcomes identify which search and compression actions were useful.
Make optional human intervention experimentally measurable: correction rate, disagreement, cost, and downstream generalization.
open_questions: Do KARL's learned search behaviors transfer to different tools, retrievers, corpus structures, and non-search agent tasks?
How much of the OOD gain survives evaluation on independently authored, post-training-cutoff questions with hidden corpora?
Can citation-entailment and contradiction penalties replace or augment nugget recall without destabilizing RL?
Which synthetic-data filters improve transfer rather than merely align generated questions to the benchmark judge?
How stable are model rankings and cost frontiers across seeds, fixed total FLOPs, hardware, and provider settings?
When does human review of synthetic questions, rewards, or compression summaries produce enough marginal validity to justify its cost?
Can a support-sensitive experiment distinguish genuinely new reasoning capabilities from reweighted rare base-model behavior?

competitive_landscape.title: Search-R1: Training LLMs to Reason and Leverage Search Engines with Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Search-R1 jointly trains reasoning and search calls with RL in question answering; KARL adds enterprise corpora, multi-task synthesis, iterative off-policy updates, learned compression, and broader test-time search.

competitive_landscape.title: DeepResearcher: Scaling Deep Research via Reinforcement Learning in Real-world Environments
competitive_landscape.difference: DeepResearcher trains long-horizon web research with RL in live environments; KARL restricts action to indexed vector search but controls private corpora and studies synthetic enterprise tasks, compression, and OAPL.

competitive_landscape.title: DR Tulu: Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics for Deep Research
competitive_landscape.difference: DR Tulu evolves task rubrics for deep-research RL to improve supervision as policies change; KARL uses largely fixed nugget outcomes and iterative data collection, leaving segment credit and judge validity less explicit.

competitive_landscape.title: SPICE: Self-Play In Corpus Environments Improves Reasoning
competitive_landscape.difference: SPICE generates and solves questions through self-play inside corpora to improve reasoning without authored labels; KARL builds a larger enterprise-search pipeline with explicit quality filters, multi-task OAPL, and six evaluation regimes.

competitive_landscape.title: NaturalReasoning: Reasoning in the Wild with 2.8M Challenging Questions
competitive_landscape.difference: NaturalReasoning scales diverse web-derived reasoning questions to 2.8 million examples for supervised or preference training; KARL generates corpus-grounded agent trajectories with tools and outcome RL rather than static question-answer data.

competitive_landscape.title: LLMs Can Learn to Reason Via Off-Policy RL
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper introduces the OAPL method for reasoning from off-policy trajectories; KARL applies and extends the recipe to segmented, tool-using, multi-task enterprise search with iterative data refresh.

competitive_landscape.title: BrowseComp-Plus: A More Fair and Transparent Evaluation Benchmark of Deep-Research Agent
competitive_landscape.difference: BrowseComp-Plus reconstructs a transparent, inspectable corpus and evidence set for deep-research evaluation; KARL trains synthetic data against that corpus and uses a bounded first-chunk configuration with an 86.5% evidence ceiling.

competitive_landscape.title: DeepScholar-Bench: A Live Benchmark and Automated Evaluation for Generative Research Synthesis
competitive_landscape.difference: DeepScholar-Bench uses live scholarly tasks and automated research-synthesis evaluation to reduce staleness; KARLBench spans more enterprise query forms but includes static public tasks, generated nuggets, and a private component.

competitive_landscape.title: WebThinker: Empowering Large Reasoning Models with Deep Research Capability
competitive_landscape.difference: WebThinker interleaves web search, navigation, and reasoning over open-web evidence; KARL narrows the tool surface to vector retrieval but performs explicit RL, synthetic enterprise training, and compute-quality analysis.

competitive_landscape.title: Value-Guided Search for Efficient Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
competitive_landscape.difference: Value-Guided Search develops learned-value allocation for reasoning traces; KARL applies the idea to long-horizon search agents and reports a BrowseComp-Plus gain from 59.6 to 70.4 with 17 candidates.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: KARL establishes a new iterative off-policy RL paradigm for enterprise knowledge agents, with synthetic multi-capability training, OOD generalization, and Pareto-optimal quality, cost, and latency against frontier proprietary models.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The system integrates six benchmark regimes, two synthetic training domains, OAPL iterations, learned compression, parallel thinking, and value-guided search; single-call KARL improves 6.3 aggregate points over GLM-4.5-Air and N=10 reaches Claude 4.6 Opus's reported 67.5 total.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The system-level integration and scale are credible novelty beyond Search-R1, DeepResearcher, SPICE, and OAPL alone. The strongest defensible result is efficient specialization plus multi-regime transfer within a common retrieval interface. Claims of broad OOD capability or decisive Pareto superiority need independent hidden tasks, non-circular judges, hardware/compute matching, seed intervals, and contamination controls; single-task non-transfer and the small single-call OOD gain materially narrow the generalization claim.

reviewer_notes: All 77 extracted pages were read, including benchmark prompts, corpus construction, price and latency methodology, synthetic-data examples, behavioral annotations, compression failures, and the optional human-preference interface. The page-53 statement that no TREC quality filter is applied was checked against the main-text quality-filter claim and page-56 example and is retained as an internal contradiction. Competitor records were checked against primary arXiv pages on 2026-08-23. Reported OOD means held out from KARL training, not out of distribution for proprietary baselines or outside the common retrieval-agent interface. No unsupported inference is made from max@k to new model support.
